If anyone received a shock or burn, medical evaluation comes before any job restart; the job waits, the person does not.

title: Turn an estimate into a quote the customer signs
mechanism_check: Estimates are internal; quotes are promises. The mechanism that loses money is the verbal quote: 'about four hundred' becomes four hundred no matter what was found.
The coordination challenge is scope edges: customers hear the number, not the assumptions — the quote must name what is included and what is not, in writing.
Profit lives in the line items: materials, labor, contingency, and the change-order clause are what keep a fixed quote from becoming free work.
improvised_tools: A one-page quote template: scope lines, materials total, labor total, exclusions, change-order clause, expiry date
The exclusions habit: every quote names what it does NOT cover (patching, painting, panel work) so 'while you are here' has a price
A signature line, even on a text message quote: 'reply YES to approve' turns a number into an agreement
steps: Convert the electrical-040 estimate into the quote template: separate lines for scope, materials, labor, and timeline.
Write the exclusions in plain language — what the price does not include is as binding as what it does.
Add the change-order clause: any work beyond the written scope gets a written price before it starts.
Put an expiry date on the quote (two weeks is honest) so material prices cannot move under you.
Present the written quote and get explicit approval — a signed page or a 'YES' reply — before the first tool comes out.
File the approved quote with the job's room sheets; it is the scope bible for every 'while you are here' conversation.
stop_conditions: Stop if the customer pushes you to start on a verbal number — no written approval, no work; the insistence is the warning.
Stop and call a licensed electrician for the quote if the scope edges into panel, service, or permitted work past your scope — price only what you can legally do.
Never sign a quote that deletes your contingency to win the bid: the cheapest quote that loses money is not a job, it is a donation.

title: Run a shadow rotation so every apprentice touches every task
mechanism_check: Apprentices plateau when they become 'the outlet guy': the mechanism is rotation — every task touched in the first months builds the whole-trade map that specialists never get.
The coordination challenge is the schedule: rotation costs the lead ten minutes of planning per week and returns a crew where anyone can cover anyone.
The failure mode is the comfort trap: the lead keeps the reliable apprentice on the easy task because the job goes faster — and the apprentice's growth stops there.
improvised_tools: A task grid on the job board: tasks down the side, apprentice names across the top, checkmarks for completed rotations
The weekly swap ritual: Monday morning, each apprentice's task changes — announced, not negotiated
The teach-back slot in the day-end huddle: the rotated apprentice explains their new task, proving the rotation worked
steps: List the job's recurring tasks on the grid: outlets, switches, fixtures, pulls, labeling, clean-up, panel schedule checks.
Assign each apprentice a different starting task; post the grid where the crew sees it every morning.
Monday: rotate everyone one column over — no one repeats a task until all are checked.
Pair each rotated apprentice with whoever did that task last week for a ten-minute handoff.
In the day-end huddle, the rotated apprentice teach-backs the new task: what they learned, what almost went wrong.
When every apprentice has checked every task, start a second rotation with harder pairings — the grid never fills permanently.
stop_conditions: Stop the rotation for any task past the apprentice's level — foundation apprentices never rotate onto panel or live-circuit work; their grid square stays blank and honest.
Stop if rotation pressure is rushing safety steps: an apprentice who skips verification to 'keep up' gets pulled off rotation until the habit is automatic.
Call a licensed electrician for any task the rotation reveals as past crew scope — the grid maps your limits, it does not erase them.
